name: Intel Corporation
monetization: Sells x86 CPUs (data center + client) while rebuilding as a US-champion foundry — recapitalized by the US government (~10%), Nvidia ($5B), SoftBank ($2B), and a $15B public share sale.
description_md: Intel is the US integrated device manufacturer attempting a dual turnaround: regain process leadership (18A ramping in 2026, 14A targeted for 2028) and build a merchant foundry serving external customers, while its product business sells Xeon CPUs into AI head-nodes and client CPUs into AI PCs. Since mid-2025 it has become a partially state-backed enterprise: the US government converted CHIPS Act grants into a ~9.9% equity stake ($8.9B), with strategic investments from Nvidia ($5B) and SoftBank ($2B) alongside.
ai_monetization_md: Intel's AI monetization today is mostly indirect: Xeon CPUs attach to GPU servers, Gaudi/GPU accelerator revenue is small, and the AI-era prize is foundry — winning advanced-node and advanced-packaging orders from AI chip designers seeking a second source to TSMC. Intel Foundry revenue was $5.8B in Q2 2026 (still only $293M external) at a $2.1B operating loss. The Nvidia partnership pairs the $5B investment with co-developed x86-RTX products and potential foundry/packaging work; High-NA EUV moved into production use at Intel in 2026, per ASML. The August 2026 $15B stock sale explicitly funds AI-chip development and foundry expansion ahead of committed external demand.
ai_strategy_md: Ride sovereign-industrial backing: convert government capital, strategic-investor capital ($8.9B USG + $5B Nvidia + $2B SoftBank), and the planned $15B equity raise into 18A/14A capacity that AI designers will need for supply-chain diversification and US-content requirements. Execute 18A (output ~25% above target in Q2 2026, +50% q/q) to prove the foundry can serve external AI customers at scale. The bet: export-control politics and TSMC concentration risk make a credible US leading-edge alternative strategically valuable enough to be paid for before the customer list exists.
risk_notes_md: **Unfunded demand:** Intel is building leading-edge capacity for external customers who largely have not signed — the inverse of the industry's committed-but-unfunded pattern (funded capacity, uncommitted demand). Foundry lost $2.1B in Q2 2026 alone. **Dilution stack:** USG ~10%, Nvidia, SoftBank, then a $15B offering (announced Aug 10, 2026; shares fell ~5%) — Intel's first public share sale since 1971. **Politicization:** a government equity holder creates procurement tailwinds but also policy risk; the stake was flagged UNVERIFIED in early drafts and is now well-documented. **Competitive:** 18A/14A must land on schedule against TSMC N2/A16.

events.title: US government converts CHIPS grants into ~9.9% Intel stake for $8.9B
events.why_it_matters: Unprecedented peacetime state equity in a US chipmaker — makes Intel the explicit national-champion foundry and puts the US government inside the AI supply chain's cap table.

events.title: Nvidia invests $5B in Intel; co-development partnership announced
events.why_it_matters: Nvidia equity-seeds its own potential second-source foundry and x86 partner — a supplier-side example of Nvidia financing its ecosystem (SoftBank added $2B in Aug 2025).

events.title: Intel announces $15B underwritten public stock offering
events.why_it_matters: Funds AI-chip and foundry expansion ahead of signed external demand; shares fell ~5%. Some analysts argued Intel should have raised far more while AI-linked equity is cheap.
